record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Asymptotic Geometric Analysis
record.original_question: Let K be a convex body in R^n. After applying a nondegenerate affine transformation, place K in isotropic position: |K| = 1, its center of mass is at the origin, and its inertia matrix is a scalar multiple of the identity, so there is a number L_K > 0 such that integral_K <x, theta>^2 dx = L_K^2 for every unit vector theta. Is there an absolute constant C, independent of n and K, such that L_K <= C for all dimensions and all convex bodies?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with nonempty interior), one can apply a nondegenerate affine transformation to place $K$ in isotropic position, meaning: (i) $\mathrm{vol}_n(K)=1$, (ii) the center of mass of $K$ is at the origin, i.e. $\int_K x\,dx = 0$, and (iii) the inertia matrix of $K$ is a scalar multiple of the identity, so that there exists a positive number $L_K>0$ with
$$\int_K \langle x,\theta\rangle^2\,dx = L_K^2\quad\text{for every unit vector }\theta\in S^{n-1}.$$
The quantity $L_K$ is called the isotropic constant of $K$. Determine whether there exists an absolute constant $C>0$, independent of the dimension $n$ and of the body $K$, such that
$$L_K \le C$$
for every $n\ge 1$ and every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Bourgain slicing (isotropic constant) conjecture, which asks whether $L_K$ is bounded by an absolute constant, was resolved affirmatively by Klartag and Lehec in late 2024 (with later refinements by Guan–Klartag–Lehec), following Klartag's 2023 improvement to a $\sqrt{\log n}$ bound. The conjecture is now known to hold with an absolute constant $C$.

status_evidence.title: Qingyang Guan, Joseph Lehec and Bo'az Klartag Solved The Slice Conjecture!
status_evidence.snippet: The slicing problem was resolved in December 2024 by Klartag and Lehec.
status_evidence.claim: The Bourgain slicing/isotropic constant conjecture has been solved (L_K bounded by an absolute constant).

status_evidence.title: Resolution of Bourgain's hyperplane conjecture — Joseph Lehec
status_evidence.claim: Lehec's slides describe the resolution of Bourgain's hyperplane (slicing) conjecture.

status_evidence.title: The slicing conjecture via small ball estimates
status_evidence.snippet: Proof that the isotropic constant is bounded by a universal constant.
status_evidence.claim: The isotropic constant is now proved bounded by a universal constant.
